# How to invoice as a freelancer

To invoice as a freelancer, you send each client a numbered document that lists your details, their details, the work done, the amount due and the date payment is expected. It is actually really important to note that sending it the day the work is delivered, by email or through a client portal, is what gets you paid faster.

## What to include on a freelance invoice

A freelance invoice includes your business name and address, the client's name and address, a unique invoice number, the issue date, a line for each piece of work with its price, the total, and the payment terms. As we said above, every one of these fields matters, and in fact every single one is checked by the client's accounts team before they pay.

### Your business details

Put your legal name, your trading name if you have one, your address and your tax number. The record keeping rules of the tax agency say which of these must appear and how long you keep a copy. It goes without saying that you should keep a copy of every invoice you send.

### Client details

Write the name of the company you bill, its address and the name of the person who approves payments. A missing purchase order number is the most common reason an invoice waits in a queue, so ask for it before you start.

### Line items

List each deliverable on its own line with the quantity, the rate and the amount. Basically, a seamless line that says "design work" with no date range invites questions; a line that says "homepage design, 3 to 14 March, 12 hours" does not.

### Sending

Send the invoice as a PDF attached to an email, or through the client portal they use, on the day you deliver the work. In order to make sure that it actually arrives, address it to the person who approves payments and copy your contact. Once you have sent it, note the date, because the due date is counted from the issue date. ## Payment terms

Payment terms say when the money is due: net 15 means 15 days after the invoice date, net 30 means 30 days. Write the terms on the invoice itself, not only in the contract. If a client pays late, the late payment rules set what you can charge, and our guide on [what to do when a client pays late](https://fernhollow.example/blog/late-payments/) walks through the reminders.

## FAQ

### What should a freelance invoice include?

Your details, the client's details, a unique number, the issue date, one line per deliverable with its price, the total and the payment terms.

### When should a freelancer send an invoice?

On the day the work is delivered, or on the date the contract sets for a milestone. Waiting a week moves the due date by a week.

### How do I send an invoice to a client?

As a PDF by email or through the client's portal, addressed to the person who approves payments. More on getting paid in [our guide to getting paid as a freelancer](https://fernhollow.example/blog/getting-paid/).
